newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK March retail sales data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK March retail sales data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to data showing UK March retail sales rose 0.3 percent month-on-month and 4.0 percent year-on-year:
"Bang in line with expectations. Still a firm set of numbers. If we look at the first quarter we've got annualised growth in retail sales of around 3-3/4 percent -- that's fairly strong growth."

"Also interesting to note that the clothing and footwear sector, as we expected, is also coming in particularly strong. It's consistent with the rest of the numbers we are seeing. The earnings numbers, employment numbers, consumer credit -- all point to a very strong consumer sector."

"(The consumer sector) is only likely to get stronger through the year as we see building society pay-outs, house prices still strong and inflation coming down, boosting real incomes. These numbers are pretty much in line with expectations."

"The UK retail sales data are unlikely to have any significant impact upon rate hike speculation. Underlying message still seems to be one of consumer resistance to higher prices. Hence fall in houshold goods consistent with the higher prices in that category shown in last week's RPI data. Nothing in this to suggest that rates will be tightened 50 basis points after the election, but doubts will persist as estimates of the building societes' windfall payments are ratcheted up. Risks remain for a faster pick-up in spending than currently anticipated."
"Small negative revision to February mah give gilts a small lift, but overall data market neutral."
